# Best waterproof Bluetooth speakers for the pool or beach

**My top pick is the JBL Charge 6.** It's IP68 (dust-tight and rated for submersion), has 20 hours of battery (28 with Playtime Boost), and doubles as a power bank. What Hi-Fi? named it best overall, and BestProducts agrees. Prices in the results run about $130 to $150.
- Buy/price links: [What Hi-Fi? listing (Walmart, Amazon, Best Buy)](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Why | Price in results |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loud pool or beach party | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, survives long immersion, and gets 40+ hours of battery. Its sound is narrow, so it's weaker if you're off to the side. | Not listed ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth) links to Amazon, Best Buy and Walmart) |
| Sound in every direction, floats | Ultimate Ears Epicboom | Tom's Guide's best overall. It's IP67 with 360° sound and 15 hours of battery. | Not listed ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)) |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears Wonderboom 4 | IP67, floats, 14 hours of battery. It's smaller and not as loud. | About $65 ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)) |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip | Good Housekeeping's best overall. It's IP68, about 0.85 lb, and the size of a soda can. Battery is 12 hours. | $100 ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)) |
| Value with a saltwater rating | Soundcore Boom 3i | IP68, floats upright, saltwater-resistant, 16 hours of battery. | $129.99, or $104 with code AFSC20 per the seller ([buy here](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-3i)) |

The Boom 3i link is an affiliate link, and the code and price come from that retailer's own page. Check them at checkout.

## Tips
- **Look for IP67 or higher.** Good Housekeeping suggests at least IPX7 for pools and beaches, and IPX8 or IP68 is ideal. For sand, you also want the dust rating (the first digit) to be 5 or 6.
- **Rinse it after use.** RTINGS notes that IP ratings don't cover corrosion from salt or chlorine. Rinse with fresh water if the manual allows it, and dry the speaker before charging.
- **Floating matters at a pool.** The Boombox 4, Epicboom and Wonderboom 4 all float, as does the Boom 3i.
- **Battery figures differ by source.** The Charge 6 is listed at 20 hours by What Hi-Fi? and 28 hours (max) by BestProducts. The higher number is likely with Playtime Boost.

If you tell me your budget and whether you want something pocketable or a party-sized speaker, I can narrow it to one.
